title: An Evening Tea Ritual
content:
An evening tea is a small reset button. It is less about caffeine and more about signaling that the day is winding down.

You do not need special tools. A kettle, a mug you like, and ten quiet minutes are enough.

Choose the right tea

Herbal blends like chamomile, mint, or rooibos are gentle at night. If you want a little warmth without a buzz, try a low caffeine oolong.

Pay attention to water

Boiling water can scorch delicate leaves. Let the kettle cool for a minute before pouring, or use water just off the boil for black tea.

Make a small setup

  • Keep a spoon and a timer nearby.
  • Use a saucer or coaster to slow down the pace.
  • Dim the light while the tea steeps.

Steeping as a pause

Set a timer for three to five minutes and use that time to tidy a surface or take a slow breath. The ritual works because it creates a tiny space between tasks.

Add one simple variation

  • A slice of lemon for brightness.
  • A pinch of cinnamon for warmth.
  • A drop of honey for softness.
Rituals do not have to be long to feel meaningful.

Over time, the cup becomes a cue. The day ends, the mind quiets, and the evening feels like it belongs to you.
